data.title: Blockchain C2 and WebSocket Exfiltration from Payment Pages
data.description: Detects payment page scripts making calls to blockchain RPC endpoints or establishing WebSocket connections to unknown servers, indicating potential e-skimmer data exfiltration via blockchain-based command-and-control infrastructure. Advanced Magecart variants observed in 2025 use a loader script on the compromised site that queries a blockchain smart contract (Ethereum, BNB Chain) to retrieve the address of a second-stage payload server, then establishes a WebSocket connection for both payload delivery and data exfiltration. This technique provides censorship-resistant C2 that cannot be disrupted through conventional domain seizure or hosting provider takedown. Detection focuses on identifying JSON-RPC calls to blockchain node endpoints (Infura, Alchemy, direct nodes) and WebSocket connections to non-payment-related servers originating from payment page context.
falsepositives: Web3-native e-commerce platforms that legitimately interact with blockchain for payment processing (e.g., cryptocurrency payment acceptance)
Customer support chat widgets using WebSocket connections on checkout pages
Real-time inventory or pricing update feeds using WebSocket on payment pages
